title: Google and UK launch Operation Blue Skies to route flights around contrails
subtitle: A £5M, 30-month program will use AI to forecast contrail formation over the North Atlantic and nudge planes up to 2,000 feet out of the way.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: The UK Department for Transport and Google announced Operation Blue Skies on August 18, 2026 — a £5 million, 30-month research program that will use Google's AI to reroute North Atlantic flights around the atmospheric conditions that produce warming contrails. The DfT is contributing £2.65 million through the Aerospace Technology Institute programme, and Google is contributing £1.4 million in kind through research, engineering time, and computing. Partners include NATS, the UK Met Office, Contrails.org, Imperial College London, and the University of Cambridge. Two operational trials of roughly four months each will run across the winters of 2026-2027 and 2027-2028, with 20 to 40 test days per winter and altitude deviations of up to 2,000 feet.

Contrails — the persistent line-shaped clouds jets leave in humid, cold air — trap heat and by the project's own estimate account for roughly a third of aviation's total climate impact. The AI forecasts where contrails will form using satellite, weather, and flight-track data, then feeds the prediction to air-traffic controllers, who move specific flights out of the affected corridor. It is the first state-backed trial to attempt contrail avoidance across an entire ocean airspace rather than a single national sector.

Google and Breakthrough Energy have run smaller contrail-avoidance pilots with American Airlines since 2023, but those covered handfuls of flights over the continental US. A full North Atlantic trial exercises the tools against the messiest real-world constraints — extra fuel burn from rerouting, cross-airline coordination across US and European carriers, and the fact that avoiding a contrail may cost a small amount of extra CO2 in exchange for a much larger reduction in near-term warming. If the results replicate at scale, contrail management is one of the few climate levers where AI does the whole loop: prediction, decision, and traffic control.

For learners, this is a useful case of AI whose value comes from a boring pipeline rather than a novel model. The wins depend on data quality (six-hour humidity forecasts), integration (getting the forecast onto the controller's screen in time), and measurement (proving the avoided contrail actually didn't form). It's the shape of most real-world AI deployment — small model, large system, and the hard part is everything around the model.
